paragraphs.text: Chapter 2. The taboo. When I got to Captain Randall's house,
Case was standing on the veranda and Blackjack was in the store with customers.
There are a lot of customers today, I said to Case.
There haven't been any customers in three weeks, said Case. Three weeks, I said?
Yes, three weeks. Said Case angrily.
I smiled and said, do you know the French priest?
I don't think he likes you or Captain Randall, I said?
Because we don't go to church.
Randall and Galluschay got angry and argued a lot about religion in the past.
And when Adams died, they had a big fight.
Now Galluschay says Randall poisoned Adams.
No, of course not, I said.
I went to take a walk in the village and I heard some people singing in a church.
I stopped outside the door and looked inside.
The priest was a tall, native man who was singing with the people.
When he saw me, he immediately stopped and pointed at me.
He stared at me and was terrified.
I was frightened and ran home.
I said nothing to Uma, but I was worried.
I did not understand what was happening and I did not like it.
On Monday, no one came to my store and I was angry.
Uma, I said, it seems that coming to my store is taboo.
That evening, I went to talk to Case.
Case, I said, I think I'm taboo here.
He said, there are no taboos on this island.
I don't like Randall, I said.
Case laughed, took a lantern and went to the village.
He came back after a quarter of an hour and sat on the veranda steps.
But don't worry, because I'll help you.
Come here tomorrow morning at nine o'clock and we'll talk to the chiefs of Phalizan.
Do you know why I'm taboo?
No, but we'll find out tomorrow morning.
The next day we went to see the chiefs in their big house.
A crowd of men, women and children stood outside the big house.
There were five chiefs and they were dressed in white.
One of them spoke to Case for a long time.
He wants to know your problem.
Tell him I'm a white man and I'm British.
I came here to work to sell things from my country.
But no one has come to my store yet.
Case translated my words or he pretended to.
When they stopped talking I asked Case.
Said Case in a low voice.
But what are they afraid of?
You know, I must be careful with these people.
I work on this island too.
I don't want any trouble with the natives.
I know you don't want any trouble.
You've never come to my house.
I'm sorry but I can't come now.
Why am I taboo for nothing?
But the natives don't want to go near you.
You know Wilchan, the natives are free to go where they want.
If they don't want to buy at your store, you can't force them.
None of these people will come to my store.
They'll trade their copra with you and you'll have all of it.
I don't speak the native language so I can't talk to these people.
This is a terrible situation and you don't care.
I can't do anything to help you.
